precepts.text: And ye my flock, the flock of my pasture, are men. The Lord uses men to lead. It has always been that way and it is never going to change. Sisters, the influencers on social media making you think the man is supposed to worship the ground you walk on will not influence the men in purple and gold. Do you want a man or do you want a boy? And sisters, when your husband gets around the brothers and comes home acting different, he is supposed to come home different: he examined himself, saw he was lacking, and came home on fire to fix his house.
precepts.point: Brothers, the same goes the other way: the moment you decide not to provide, not to be the man God told you to be, watch what happens to your household. It is a domino effect. Some of you brothers did not want a wife; you wanted a mama.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
“And ye my flock, the flock of my pasture, are men, and I am your God, saith the Lord God.” The Lord uses men to lead. It has always been that way and it is never going to change. You will not change the order of things just because you are weak, or scared of your wife.

Sisters, the beta men on social media are influencing you, making you think the man is supposed to worship the ground you walk on. That will not influence the men in purple and gold. We are not worried about being called names, narcissist or misogynist. The question is, do you want a man or do you want a boy?

When your husband gets around the brothers and comes home acting different, he is supposed to. He examines himself, sees he is lacking, and comes home on fire to fix his house, with a little more pep in his step and a little more to say. The same goes when he has been rebuked for adultery or for not dealing with his wife the right way: he is supposed to move different. It works in every area if he truly believes.

This is why there is an attack on the household. Satan and his people know that to destroy us they have to attack our foundation, and the foundation is the home. Paul warned that in the last days perilous times would come, with those “Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof”, and “of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts.” They get in through the phone and the conversations, whoever is influencing them. We are building a nation, and if we are not strong on the home front, we will not get off the ground.

precepts.text: I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
precepts.point: I will seek that which was lost: that's our people. And bring again that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken: we were broken. And will strengthen that which was sick: we're the sick ones. But I will destroy the fat and the strong: I'm going to destroy the nations. I will feed them with judgment.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“For thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I, even I, will both search my sheep, and seek them out.” Who is that I? Christ. And Christ said who he came for: “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

That is what Christ was doing, seeking out the lost sheep of Israel, and that is what Paul and the apostles were doing after him. That was the great commission in Matthew 28:19.

So when Ezekiel says “I will seek that which was lost”, that's our people. The lost sheep Christ was sent to are the same sheep God promised to search out and deliver “out of all places where they have been scattered in the cloudy and dark day”: all places, countries and lands.

precepts.text: He shall call to the heavens from above: that's the angels he's calling to. And to the earth: the earth are the prophets, you and me on the earth. Gather my saints together unto me, those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice: that's the twelve tribes of Israel. So he's telling the prophets, gather the twelve tribes, and he's telling the angels, gather the twelve tribes.

And will strengthen that which was sick: we're the sick ones. But I will destroy the fat and the strong: I'm going to destroy the nations. I will feed them with judgment.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
Ezekiel says God will search his sheep and gather them from the countries. Who does the gathering? “He shall call to the heavens from above, and to the earth, that he may judge his people.” He calls to the heavens from above: those are the angels he's calling to. And to the earth: the earth are the prophets, you and me on the earth.

“Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” Those are the twelve tribes of Israel. So he's telling the prophets, gather the twelve tribes, and he's telling the angels, gather the twelve tribes.

That is the promise of Ezekiel 34: “I will bring them out from the people, and gather them from the countries, and will bring them to their own land, and feed them upon the mountains of Israel.” The good pasture is the kingdom.

precepts.text: And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds. He said gather everybody, all people? No.
precepts.point: I will seek that which was lost: that's our people. And bring again that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken: we were broken. And will strengthen that which was sick: we're the sick ones. But I will destroy the fat and the strong: I'm going to destroy the nations. I will feed them with judgment.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” These are the angels of Psalms 50, called from the heavens to gather.

Did he say gather everybody, all people? No. They gather his elect, and his elect are Israel. It's the same gathering Ezekiel spoke of: “so will I seek out my sheep, and will deliver them out of all places where they have been scattered in the cloudy and dark day.” The four winds are all the places, countries and lands where our people were scattered.

The prophets gather on the earth, the angels gather from the heavens, and it is the elect, the sheep of the house of Israel, who are gathered.

precepts.text: For Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel mine elect. So there's no contradiction from the New Testament and the Old Testament; the contradiction comes from these false pastors, these hireling pastors.
precepts.point: I will seek that which was lost: that's our people. And bring again that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken: we were broken. And will strengthen that which was sick: we're the sick ones. But I will destroy the fat and the strong: I'm going to destroy the nations. I will feed them with judgment.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
Who are the elect the angels gather in Matthew 24? Isaiah answers: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name.” Israel is God's elect.

So there's no contradiction between the New Testament and the Old Testament. Christ was sent to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, the angels gather the elect, and the elect is Israel. Ezekiel's sheep, Matthew's elect and Isaiah's elect are the same people.

The contradiction comes from these false pastors, these hireling pastors, who tell the people it is everybody. The Lord said: “I will seek that which was lost, and bring again that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken, and will strengthen that which was sick.” That's our people: we were broken, we're the sick ones. “but I will destroy the fat and the strong”: he is going to destroy the nations. “I will feed them with judgment.”

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“Praise ye the Lord. Sing unto the Lord a new song, and his praise in the congregation of saints.” The saints are the twelve tribes God gathers.

“Let Israel rejoice in him that made him”: because we have not been rejoicing in our creator, we've been rejoicing in the white man. “let the children of Zion be joyful in their King”: for so long we've been joyful in the white man.

“For the Lord taketh pleasure in his people: he will beautify the meek with salvation.” He doesn't take pleasure in all races on the planet, only in his people.

“Let the saints be joyful in glory: let them sing aloud upon their beds.” That's the rest right there. It is what Ezekiel promised the gathered sheep: “there shall they lie in a good fold, and in a fat pasture shall they feed upon the mountains of Israel. I will feed my flock, and I will cause them to lie down, saith the Lord God.”

precepts.text: I will set up one shepherd over them, my servant David, and he shall feed them.
precepts.point: Fear thou not, O my servant Jacob: what he says will happen makes us afraid, so we increase our faith by remembering this body is a shell. I will save thee from afar and thy seed from the land of their captivity, and Jacob shall return and be in rest and none shall make him afraid. Though I make a full end of all nations, the extras born in vain with Esau the villain, I will not make a full end of thee, but correct thee in measure and not leave thee altogether unpunished.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
Jeremiah says Israel “shall serve the Lord their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up unto them.” Ezekiel says the same of the last days: “And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd.”

One shepherd over the whole nation, and that shepherd is David. After Israel has abided many days without a king, the Lord himself sets David up over them, to feed them.

That is part of the promise that comes at the end of the exile and tribulation: the yoke broken from our neck, the strangers no longer serving themselves of us, Jacob returned to rest and quiet with none to make him afraid, and one shepherd, David, raised up over Israel under the Lord their God.

precepts.text: The flock of my pasture are men; the shepherds and saviors of the nation are men.
precepts.point: A sister helping to build up other sisters new in the congregation is right, and the sisters bless the nation with real talents, raising the children in the commandments, and the aged women teaching the young women. But teaching and leading the nation is not the place the Most High set for her.

note.label: Numbers 27: The Daughters of Zelophehad and the Ordination of Joshua

precepts.why:
Moses prayed that the congregation of the Lord be not as sheep which have no shepherd, and the Lord says who His flock is: “And ye my flock, the flock of my pasture, are men, and I am your God, saith the Lord God.”

The flock of His pasture are men, and the shepherds and saviors of the nation are men. That is why Moses asked for a man to lead them out and bring them in.

precepts.text: They shall know that the Most High is with them, and that the house of Israel are his people, the children of God being spoken of.
precepts.point: Caiaphas prophesied that one man should die for the people, speaking not of himself but from the prophecies he knew in Isaiah 53 and the Psalms. That nation he must die for is Israel, and "not for that nation only" means Christ would also gather the children of God scattered abroad, the twelve tribes, not the Gentiles the Christians claim.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
Who are the children of God that were scattered abroad? “Thus shall they know that I the Lord their God am with them, and that they, even the house of Israel, are my people, saith the Lord God. And ye my flock, the flock of my pasture, are men, and I am your God”.

The house of Israel are his people, his flock. The children of God being spoken of are the house of Israel, and gathering them in one is gathering the scattered tribes.
